newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS DOWNS SELES TO CLAIM NINTH TITLE OF YEAR.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS DOWNS SELES TO CLAIM NINTH TITLE OF YEAR.

text.p: Former number one Monica Seles could not stop the Martina Hingis juggernaut on Sunday as the teen queen of tennis claimed her ninth title of the year.
The top-ranked Hingis, clearly in a league of her own these days, outgunned the second-seeded Seles 7-6 (7-4) 6-4 in the final of the Tohsiba Tennis Classic.
"She's just playing some great tennis," Seles said of Hingis after the exciting one hour and 14 minute contest.
"Steffi (Graf) was in that zone, I was in that zone. She right now is in that zone."
The remarkable 16-year-old Swiss sensation, who claimed the Australian Open and Wimbledon titles this year, ran her 1997 match record to 54-1 and a perfect 27-0 on hardcourts.
And against Seles, who ruled the women's tennis world earlier in the decade, Hingis took her record to 5-0, including three wins in finals this year.
"I think Monica played her best tennis ever against me. Once I think she's gonna beat me but I'm not looking forward to that day," said the precocious teenager of her once unbeatable opponent.
Hingis, who earned $79,000 for the victory, said she does not think about her amazing record or whether anyone out there can beat here right now.

"You never know whats going to happen," said Hingis, whose only loss this year was to Iva Majoli in the French Open final. "You try to keep going. It's another challenge, you just want to keep winning."
The way she is going, Hingis just might make a run at her namesake's record. In 1983, Martina Navratilova rolled to an 86-1 mark, while capturing 16 titles.
"You just feel it," the third-ranked Seles said of the confidence exuded by Hingis.
"She has the confidence to go for shots and they always go in," added Seles, who is still looking for her first title of the year.
Seles pounded out her usual punishing ground attack, but Hingis withstood everything the second seed threw at her.

Seles had chances to claim the first set following service breaks that put her in front 4-3 and 5-4. But twice the top seed broke back to level the score at 5-5 as Seles double-faulted away the 10th game.
In the tie-break, Hingis trailed 0-2 before storming to a 5-2 advantage.
"It was really important. I got ahead pretty early and was holding on," Hingis said of the breaker in which Seles battled back to 5-4.
From there, however, Seles made two unforced errors to hand Hingis the set.
"A couple times she had to make some good shots, but I gave her too many free points," Seles said. "She wasn't giving away free points."
The second set was just as spirited as Seles fought off three breaks points in the opening game and three more in the seventh to go ahead 4-3 on serve.
At 4-4, Hingis got the lone break when Seles ripped a forehand beyond the baseline and the top seed served a love game to end the showdown.
"It was a great match," Seles said. "We had some great rallies. I had some chances in the first set but she just played better in the key points."
Still, Seles said she has had fun playing the new number one, despite the outcomes.
"We played so many matches in a short period of time, each match I enjoyed playing and it's been very positive."
